authoring.question: e-10998
authoring.value:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $\mathbf{a},$ $\mathbf{b},$ $\mathbf{c},$ and  $\mathbf{d}{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043085/assets/0563d565dff1928d21da21ad832fad37f94fb385ddb8a805423ae2577ae9434c.png)

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M{:}$

$$
V = | \det(M) |
$$

Notice that the $2$nd row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $2$nd row of the $3 \times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot 1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(15+4) \\  & =-57.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V = | \det(M) | = |-57| = 57.
$$
